attention.description: Errors and warnings in the shop’s operation

processDown.title: {{process}} is not responding
processDown.what: The process has not sent a health signal for over 45 seconds: it is stopped, has exited with an error or has lost its connection to Redis.
processDown.whyWorker: The worker runs background jobs: delivering paid subscriptions, processing events, notifications, broadcasts, emails and backups. While it is down, jobs accumulate in the queue.
processDown.whyScheduler: The scheduler starts scheduled jobs: payment checks, automatic backups, scheduled broadcasts, cleanup of outdated data. While it is down, these jobs do not run.
processDown.fix: Check the container state and its logs, and restart it if needed. Queued jobs run once the process recovers.

hostDiskFull.title: Server disk is almost full
hostDiskFull.what: The server disk is 90% full or more.
hostDiskFull.why: Without free space, the database, logs and backups cannot be written. The shop may stop and data may be corrupted.
hostDiskFull.fix: Delete outdated backups, logs and unused Docker images (docker system prune), or increase the disk size.

hostMemoryHigh.title: Server memory is nearly exhausted
hostMemoryHigh.what: Server memory is 95% used or more.
hostMemoryHigh.why: When memory runs out, the system terminates processes: the shop, the database or Redis may stop.
hostMemoryHigh.fix: Identify the processes using the most memory (docker stats). Reduce the number of worker and api processes or add memory to the server.

eventLoopLag.title: {{process}} is responding slowly
eventLoopLag.what: The 99th percentile of the process’s event loop delay exceeds 500 ms.
eventLoopLag.why: Dashboard and cabinet requests, bot replies and background jobs run slowly or time out.
eventLoopLag.fix: Check CPU load and the process logs, and restart the process if needed. If the delay recurs under load, add processes or server resources.

outboxStuck.title: The event queue is not being processed
outboxStuck.sub_one: {{formatted}} event waiting in the queue for longer than {{duration}}
outboxStuck.sub_other: {{formatted}} events waiting in the queue for longer than {{duration}}
outboxStuck.what: Shop events have been waiting for processing for over 5 minutes.
outboxStuck.why: Until the queue is processed, the event log is not updated, admin and customer notifications are not sent, referral rewards are not granted and loyalty discounts are not recalculated.
outboxStuck.fix: The most likely cause is a stopped worker. If it is running, check its logs for event processing errors. Events are not lost and will be processed once the queue recovers.

panelUnavailable.title: Connection to Remnawave lost
panelUnavailable.sub: The panel does not respond or the reply is not recognized
panelUnavailable.what: The node list could not be retrieved from the Remnawave panel: the panel did not respond or returned a response in an unknown format.
panelUnavailable.why: While the panel is unavailable, subscriptions are not issued or renewed, and sync and device management do not work. A changed response format may break individual features.
panelUnavailable.fix: Check that the panel is reachable and that the URL and token in the settings are correct. If the panel was updated recently, make sure this shop version supports it. Details are in the api logs.

nodeOffline.title: Connection to node “{{node}}” lost
nodeOffline.what: The node is enabled in the Remnawave panel but is not connected.
nodeOffline.why: Customers on this node cannot use the VPN, and new connections to it are not possible.
nodeOffline.fix: Check the node server and its status in the Remnawave panel.

gatewayFailures.title: Payment failures via {{gateway}}
gatewayFailures.sub_one: {{formatted}} failed payment in the last hour
gatewayFailures.sub_other: {{formatted}} failed payments in the last hour
gatewayFailures.what: 5 or more payments through this gateway failed in the last hour.
gatewayFailures.why: Customers cannot pay by this method, and the shop loses revenue.
gatewayFailures.fix: Check the gateway settings and its merchant dashboard: keys, shop status, limits. If the failure is on the gateway’s side, disable it temporarily.

smtpFailed.title: Email sending failure
smtpFailed.what: The last attempt to send an email through this SMTP server failed. The item clears after the first successful send or after a day, even if the error is not fixed.
smtpFailed.why: Until sending works, customers do not receive cabinet sign-in codes, subscription notifications or broadcast emails.
smtpFailed.fix: Send a test email from the email settings to see the error. Common causes: a wrong password, a closed port, the provider’s sending limit.

backupFailed.title: Backup failed
backupFailed.what: The last backup run of this type failed.
backupFailed.why: Without a current backup, data since the last successful backup cannot be restored after a server or database failure.
backupFailed.fix: Open backups: the run record shows the error. Common causes are insufficient disk space and missing folder permissions. Once fixed, start a backup manually.

backupOverdue.title: Backups are not being created on schedule
backupOverdue.never: No backups since it was enabled
backupOverdue.what: Automatic backups are enabled, but there has been no successful backup for longer than the set interval.
backupOverdue.why: Without a current backup, data since the last successful backup cannot be restored after a server or database failure.
backupOverdue.fix: Check that the worker and scheduler are running; they create backups. Then start a backup manually and make sure it succeeds.

broadcastFailed.title: Broadcast “{{name}}” stopped with an error
broadcastFailed.what: The broadcast stopped due to an error; some recipients did not receive the message.
broadcastFailed.why: Customers the broadcast did not reach will not hear about the news or offer.
broadcastFailed.fix: Open the broadcast: it shows the cause and the number of messages sent. Once the error is fixed, sending can be retried for the remaining recipients.

broadcastStalled.title: Broadcast “{{name}}” is stuck
broadcastStalled.what: The broadcast has not progressed for over 15 minutes, and the automatic restart did not help.
broadcastStalled.why: Until the broadcast resumes, the remaining recipients will not receive the message.
broadcastStalled.fix: Check that the worker and scheduler are running; they process broadcasts. If they are, check the worker logs. The broadcast can be canceled if needed.

paidNotFulfilled.title: Paid but not delivered
paidNotFulfilled.sub_one: {{formatted}} order waiting for delivery over 10 minutes
paidNotFulfilled.sub_other: {{formatted}} orders waiting for delivery over 10 minutes
paidNotFulfilled.what: The payment was received, but the subscription has not been issued within 10 minutes.
paidNotFulfilled.why: The customer paid but has no access. This leads to support requests and refunds.
paidNotFulfilled.fix: The shop retries delivery automatically. If the item persists, check the panel connection and the worker, then fulfill the order manually in transactions.

stalePending.title: Payments awaiting confirmation
stalePending.sub_one: {{formatted}} transaction without a reply for longer than 15 minutes
stalePending.sub_other: {{formatted}} transactions without a reply for longer than 15 minutes
stalePending.what: 5 or more transactions have been pending for over 15 minutes: the gateway has sent neither a confirmation nor a refusal.
stalePending.why: These are usually abandoned payments. A large number may mean the gateway is not delivering payment notifications and paid orders are not being fulfilled.
stalePending.fix: Check the status of these payments in the gateway dashboard and verify the notification (webhook) URL.

emailUndeliverable.title: Emails are not reaching recipients
emailUndeliverable.sub_one: {{formatted}} address rejected in the last day
emailUndeliverable.sub_other: {{formatted}} addresses rejected in the last day
emailUndeliverable.what: In the last day, mail servers permanently rejected emails to 10 or more addresses, usually because the mailbox does not exist or was deleted.
emailUndeliverable.why: The shop stops sending to such addresses until the customer signs in with an email code again or links the email anew. A spike usually indicates fake sign-ups or a broadcast to an outdated list.
emailUndeliverable.fix: Check where these users signed up from. If an address is valid, the mark can be cleared manually in the user’s card.

expiringPaid.title: Expiring subscriptions
expiringPaid.urgent: {{base}}, {{urgent}} of them within the next day
expiringPaid.what: Paid subscriptions that expire in the next 7 days.
expiringPaid.why: Without a reminder, some customers will not renew. This revenue can still be retained.
expiringPaid.fix: Review retention and, if needed, send a broadcast with a reminder or a renewal promo code.

apiTokenExpiring.title: API token “{{name}}” expires soon
apiTokenExpiring.what: The API token expires in the next 7 days.
apiTokenExpiring.why: Once it expires, integrations using the token stop working.
apiTokenExpiring.fix: Issue a new token with the same permissions, replace it in the integration and revoke the old one.

botWebhook.title: Telegram bot webhook is not working
botWebhook.what: Telegram reports an error delivering updates to the bot, or the webhook is not set.
botWebhook.why: The bot does not receive messages or button presses, and customers cannot use it.
botWebhook.fix: Check the webhook URL in the bot settings and that the server is reachable from the internet over HTTPS. Restarting the bot usually helps.

planSquadsMissing.title: Plan “{{name}}” is off sale
planSquadsMissing.subOne: A squad of the plan is missing in Remnawave
planSquadsMissing.subMany: Squads of the plan are missing in Remnawave
planSquadsMissing.what: The plan uses squads that do not exist in the Remnawave panel.
planSquadsMissing.why: The panel does not create users with a nonexistent squad. The plan is hidden from sale in the bot and the cabinet; trials, promocodes and admin grants on this plan do not work.
planSquadsMissing.fix: Open the plan and replace its squads with ones that exist in the panel. The plan returns to sale within a minute.

guide.title: How pricing works
guide.intro: You set prices once in the anchor currency and the rest are calculated automatically. Where the calculation doesn’t suit you, pin the price in that currency by hand.
guide.saveTip: Changes in the table take effect when you press “Save”.
guide.calculationBody: The base price is multiplied by the currency’s rate, the result is rounded and then raised to the price ending. If that’s below the minimum amount, the minimum is used. Each currency’s settings are in “Currency rates”.
guide.calculationExample: Example: base 4.99 USD, RUB rate 85, rounding to a whole number, ending 99. 4.99 × 85 = 424.15, rounded to 424, raised to the ending: 499 ₽.
guide.anchorColumnBody: The base price is the number you enter. The anchor currency column shows the final price for the customer, with rounding and the ending already applied. This column can’t be edited or pinned; to change it, change the base price.
guide.anchorColumnExample: Example: base 4.20 USD, with ending 99 and rounding to 2 decimals for USD. The customer sees 4.99 $.
guide.pinBody: To set your own price in a currency, type a value into its column or press the pin, which pins the current price. A pinned price doesn’t change with the rate or the base price unless a bulk change rescales or resets it. Rounding and the ending don’t apply to it; a rescaled pin is rounded by the currency’s rounding, still without the ending. The minimum amount still applies. Pressing the pin again removes it and the price follows the rate again.
guide.pinExample: Example: you want exactly 399 ₽ a month. Type 399 into the RUB column. If the rate goes from 85 to 95, the price stays 399 ₽ while unpinned prices are recalculated.
guide.bulkBody: Changes the base prices of all plans, all add-ons or one plan. Three methods: by percent, one price for all, or a duration ladder. Pinned prices can be kept, rescaled by the same ratio as the base price, or reset to follow the rate. A list of changes with the percent difference is shown before applying.
guide.bulkExample: Example: “by percent” with 10 raises base prices by 10%, −10 lowers them by 10%. A base of 4.99 becomes 5.49.
guide.ladderBody: Every duration is priced from one base duration: its daily price times the days, then the duration’s discount. A negative discount is a markup, for when short durations should cost more per day. The base is picked from the durations in the selection: 30 days if there is one, otherwise the shortest. The ladder skips add-ons, which have no duration, and the free trial.
guide.ladderExample: Example: a 30-day base at 300 ₽. With 10% off for 90 days: 300 × 3 × 0.9 = 810 ₽. With a −40% markup for 7 days: 300 × 7 / 30 × 1.4 = 98 ₽.
guide.anchorSwitchBody: Base prices and rates are recalculated for the new currency, and its rate becomes 1. A price pinned in the new currency becomes the base price, since the anchor column can’t be pinned. Loyalty tier thresholds and the anchor amounts of past payments are rescaled too. Final prices may shift slightly because of rounding, so you see the list of changes before applying.
guide.anchorSwitchExample: Example: the anchor changes from USD to RUB at a rate of 85. A base price of 4.99 becomes 424.15 and the RUB rate becomes 1.

guide.title: How the loyalty program works
guide.intro: A customer automatically gets a discount for the total of their purchases: the more they’ve paid, the higher the tier. While the program is off, nobody gets this discount.
guide.tiersBody: Each tier is a purchase total threshold and a discount percent. The customer gets the highest tier whose threshold they’ve reached. Thresholds and percents must grow from tier to tier. Amounts are in the anchor currency; when it changes, thresholds are recalculated at the rate.
guide.tiersExample: Example: tiers 10 $ — 3%, 30 $ — 5%, 50 $ — 7%. A customer paid 35 $, so the discount is 5%. Exactly 50 $ already gives 7%.
guide.windowBody: Sets how far back purchases count. “All time” counts everything the customer ever paid. With a limited period, old purchases stop counting and the discount can go down. The total includes paid purchases, renewals, plan changes and add-ons, at the price after all discounts. Refunds don’t count.
guide.windowExample: Example: a 12-month period. A customer paid 60 $ two years ago and 20 $ this month. Only 20 $ counts, so the discount is 3%.
guide.combineBody: The loyalty discount doesn’t add up with the personal discount or a promocode’s purchase discount: the largest one applies. A plan’s sale applies separately, one after the other with this discount.
guide.combineExample: Example: loyalty 5% and personal 10%, so 10% applies. If the plan also has a 20% sale, a 100 $ price becomes 72 $: minus 20%, then minus 10%.
guide.recalculationBody: A customer’s discount updates after their purchase, renewal, plan change or refund. For all customers at once it updates after settings are saved or reset, and every day at 03:00 UTC. The nightly run accounts for purchases leaving the period.
guide.recalculationExample: Example: you switch the program off and save. After the recalculation the loyalty discount is zero for all customers.
guide.excludeBody: A single customer can be excluded from the program on their card. Their loyalty discount becomes 0%; the personal discount and promocodes keep working.
guide.excludeExample: Example: an employee with a 50% personal discount shouldn’t be in the program: exclude them and the 50% stays.
